name: Batch data extraction
summary: Scheduled pulls of data from a source system (database or application) into the platform.
description: Involves scheduling reliable pulls from operational databases or applications into a raw landing zone. Key decisions include full vs incremental extraction strategy (watermarks, snapshots), extraction windows that respect source load, and idempotent re-runs. Typical pitfalls are silent source schema drift and late-arriving or updated rows breaking incremental logic.

name: API extraction
summary: Ingesting data from REST, GraphQL, or SOAP APIs, typically SaaS applications like Salesforce or Stripe.
description: Involves building resilient extractors against REST, GraphQL, or SOAP APIs, usually for SaaS systems. Key decisions include pagination and incremental cursor strategy, rate-limit and retry handling, and auth token lifecycle management. Typical pitfalls are undocumented API quirks, breaking vendor API changes, and backfill limits on historical data.

name: File-drop ingestion
summary: Ingesting files landed on FTP/SFTP or object storage, such as partner feeds and exports.

name: Web scraping pipeline
summary: Crawling and scraping public or partner web data into the platform.

name: Change data capture (CDC)
summary: Log-based replication of OLTP database changes using tools like Debezium, DMS, or GoldenGate.
description: Involves capturing row-level changes from OLTP transaction logs and delivering them downstream with minimal source impact. Key decisions include tool choice (Debezium, DMS, GoldenGate), initial snapshot strategy, and how to handle schema evolution and deletes. Typical pitfalls are log retention gaps forcing resnapshots, out-of-order events, and replication slot pressure on the source.

name: Streaming ingestion
summary: Continuous event intake into a message broker such as Kafka, Kinesis, or Pub/Sub.
description: Involves standing up continuous event intake into a broker such as Kafka, Kinesis, or Pub/Sub. Key decisions include topic and partition design, serialization format and schema registry usage, and delivery semantics (at-least-once vs exactly-once). Typical pitfalls are unbounded consumer lag, hot partitions, and uncontrolled schema evolution by producers.

name: IoT / sensor telemetry ingestion
summary: High-volume device data ingestion with edge concerns such as MQTT and gateways.

name: Log & clickstream collection
summary: Collecting application/server logs and product analytics events in the Segment style.

name: Third-party data onboarding
summary: Onboarding purchased or external datasets such as weather, market, or enrichment feeds.

name: SaaS connector rollout
summary: Standing up a managed EL tool like Fivetran or Airbyte across multiple sources.

name: Database migration / upgrade
summary: Engine-to-engine or major-version database move, such as Oracle to Postgres or MySQL 5 to 8.

name: Warehouse migration
summary: Replatforming a warehouse, e.g. Teradata or Redshift to Snowflake, BigQuery, or Databricks.

name: Cloud data migration
summary: Moving an on-prem data estate to the cloud via lift-and-shift or re-architecture.

name: Lake → lakehouse migration
summary: Moving Hive or raw-Parquet estates onto Iceberg or Delta with proper catalogs.

name: Mainframe / legacy offload
summary: Liberating COBOL/VSAM/DB2 data from mainframes into modern platforms.

name: Cross-region / DR replication
summary: Geo-replication, disaster-recovery copies, and data sovereignty splits.

name: Data archiving & retention move
summary: Relocating cold data to cheap storage tiers with defined retrieval SLAs.

name: ETL pipeline build
summary: Classic transform-before-load pipeline construction.

name: ELT transformation layer
summary: Warehouse-native SQL transformation in the dbt/SQLMesh style, including the add-a-new-transformation brownfield flow.
description: Involves building a warehouse-native SQL transformation layer (dbt or SQLMesh style) from staging through marts, including the brownfield flow of adding new transformations to an existing project. Key decisions include layering conventions, incremental materialization strategies, and testing and documentation standards. Typical pitfalls are model sprawl without ownership and expensive full-refresh patterns.

name: Dimensional model (Kimball)
summary: Star schemas with facts, dimensions, and slowly changing dimension handling.
description: Involves designing star schemas with conformed dimensions, fact tables at an explicit grain, and slowly changing dimension handling. Key decisions include grain declaration per fact, SCD type per dimension, and surrogate vs natural keys. Typical pitfalls are mixed-grain facts, mishandled late-arriving dimensions, and silent fan-out in joins.

name: Data Vault model
summary: Hubs, links, and satellites modelling for audit-heavy enterprises.

name: 3NF / enterprise model (Inmon)
summary: Normalized enterprise data model in the Inmon tradition.

name: Semantic / metrics layer
summary: Governed metric definitions using tools like MetricFlow, Cube, or Looker models.

name: Data cleansing & standardization
summary: Fixing formats, codes, addresses, and units at scale.

name: Entity resolution / deduplication
summary: Matching customers or products across systems to deduplicate records.

name: Master data management (MDM)
summary: Golden records with a stewardship workflow.

name: Aggregation / reporting marts
summary: Purpose-built marts and summary tables for downstream consumers.

name: Data warehouse design & build
summary: Standing up or restructuring the central analytical store.
description: Involves standing up or restructuring the central analytical store, from platform selection through schema, workload, and access design. Key decisions include the compute and storage sizing model, zone and schema layout, and workload isolation between loads and BI. Typical pitfalls are unmanaged cost growth and modelling the warehouse around a single team's queries.

name: Data lake build
summary: Raw and curated zones on object storage.

name: Lakehouse implementation
summary: Table formats plus catalog plus compute on the lake.
description: Involves implementing open table formats (Iceberg, Delta, Hudi) with a catalog and query engines over object storage. Key decisions include table format and catalog choice, medallion zone layout, and compaction and maintenance strategy. Typical pitfalls are small-file explosions, catalog and engine compatibility gaps, and skipping table maintenance jobs.

name: Operational data store (ODS)
summary: Near-real-time integrated operational copy of source data.

name: OLTP schema design
summary: Application database modelling.

name: Storage layout & partitioning optimization
summary: Partitioning, clustering, and file-size compaction on the storage layer.

name: Platform cost optimization
summary: FinOps for data: warehouse credits, storage tiers, and egress costs.

name: Data platform infrastructure (IaC)
summary: Terraform or Pulumi provisioning of the data estate.

name: Stream processing pipeline
summary: Stateful transforms on streams using Flink, Spark Structured Streaming, or Kafka Streams.
description: Involves building stateful transformations over streams with Flink, Spark Structured Streaming, or Kafka Streams. Key decisions include event-time vs processing-time semantics, windowing and watermark strategy, and state backend and checkpointing design. Typical pitfalls are unbounded state growth, mishandled late data, and painful recovery from bad deploys.

name: Event-driven architecture
summary: Broker topology, schema registry, and producer/consumer contracts.

name: Real-time analytics serving
summary: Sub-second OLAP with Pinot, Druid, or ClickHouse behind dashboards and APIs.

name: Streaming enrichment & joins
summary: Joining streams with reference data in-flight.

name: CDC-to-stream fanout
summary: Turning database changes into consumable event streams.

name: Complex event processing (CEP)
summary: Pattern detection over event windows for use cases like fraud and alerting.

name: Event sourcing / CQRS data layer
summary: Event-log-as-truth with materialized read models.

name: Real-time feature computation
summary: Low-latency ML feature computation from streams.

name: Orchestrator rollout / migration
summary: Standing up Airflow, Dagster, or Prefect, or migrating between orchestrators.
description: Involves standing up Airflow, Dagster, or Prefect (or migrating between them) as the scheduling backbone for pipelines. Key decisions include the deployment model (managed vs self-hosted), DAG design and dependency conventions, and migration sequencing for existing jobs. Typical pitfalls are scheduler resource contention, hidden cross-DAG dependencies, and big-bang migrations.

name: Pipeline CI/CD
summary: Tests, environments, and deployment automation for data code.

name: Data testing framework adoption
summary: Wiring Great Expectations, Soda, or dbt tests into pipelines.

name: Data contracts rollout
summary: Producer/consumer schema contracts with enforcement.

name: Observability & monitoring rollout
summary: Freshness, volume, and distribution monitors with alerting and on-call.

name: Environment & release strategy
summary: Dev/staging/prod data environments, sandboxing, and promotion.

name: Backfill & reprocessing framework
summary: Safe historical reprocessing at scale.

name: Pipeline performance tuning
summary: Making slow pipelines fast by addressing skew, spill, and incremental strategies.

name: PII handling initiative
summary: Discovery, classification, anonymization strategy (on-the-fly vs at-rest, role-based masking vs static), and rollout.
description: A stage-gated initiative covering PII discovery, classification, an anonymization strategy (on-the-fly vs at-rest, role-based dynamic masking vs static), and phased rollout. Key decisions include scanning tooling, the masking approach per data class, and how policies bind to roles. Typical pitfalls are PII leaking through derived tables and exports, and masking that breaks joins or analytical utility.

name: GDPR / CCPA compliance
summary: Right-to-be-forgotten, consent propagation, and DSAR handling.

name: Data classification program
summary: Sensitivity tiers applied across the estate.

name: Access control (RBAC/ABAC) rollout
summary: Roles, row/column-level security, and grants automation.

name: Masking & tokenization
summary: Static and dynamic masking, tokenization vaults, and test-data safety.

name: Encryption at rest / in transit
summary: Key management, TDE, and TLS enforcement.

name: Audit logging & access review
summary: Tracking who touched what, with attestation cycles.

name: Retention & deletion policy
summary: Lifecycle rules with legal holds.

name: Data catalog rollout
summary: DataHub, OpenMetadata, or Collibra deployment plus adoption.

name: Data lineage initiative
summary: Column and table lineage capture (OpenLineage) and use.

name: Data quality framework
summary: Quality dimensions, SLAs, issue workflow, and scorecards.
description: A stage-gated initiative defining quality dimensions, SLAs, detection rules, an issue-resolution workflow, and scorecards. Key decisions include which dimensions to measure per dataset tier, who owns failures, and where checks run in the pipeline. Typical pitfalls are alert fatigue from unowned checks and measuring quality without a remediation path.

name: Data governance operating model
summary: Stewardship roles, councils, and policies.

name: Data residency / sovereignty
summary: Keeping data in-jurisdiction across the stack.

name: BI dashboard build
summary: Curated dashboards on governed data.
description: Involves delivering curated dashboards on governed data with a BI tool, from requirements through semantic modelling and rollout. Key decisions include tool fit, shared metric definitions across dashboards, and refresh and caching strategy. Typical pitfalls are dashboard sprawl with conflicting numbers and slow dashboards built on unmodelled queries.

name: Self-service analytics enablement
summary: Governed exploration for analysts via a semantic layer and training.

name: Embedded analytics
summary: Analytics inside a customer-facing product.

name: Operational reporting automation
summary: Replacing manual Excel and email reporting with automation.

name: KPI / metric standardization
summary: Establishing one definition of metrics like revenue across the company.

name: Data API / data-as-a-product
summary: Serving governed data via APIs with SLAs.

name: Reverse ETL / data activation
summary: Syncing warehouse data into SaaS tools like CRM, ads, and support platforms.
description: Involves syncing modelled warehouse data into operational SaaS tools (CRM, ads, support) with a reverse-ETL platform. Key decisions include sync frequency and mode (full vs diff), field mapping and identity resolution, and API quota management on the targets. Typical pitfalls are overwriting operator-edited fields in the destination and silent partial sync failures.

name: Data sharing / clean rooms
summary: Cross-org sharing via Snowflake shares or clean rooms.

name: Data monetization
summary: Packaging data for external sale.

name: Feature store implementation
summary: Offline and online features with point-in-time correctness.

name: ML training data pipeline
summary: Labeled and curated training sets with versioning.

name: MLOps platform
summary: Experiment tracking, model registry, and deployment automation.

name: Model serving data flows
summary: Online inference data paths and caching.

name: Vector database / RAG pipeline
summary: Chunking, embedding, and retrieval for LLM applications.
description: Involves building the chunking, embedding, indexing, and retrieval path that grounds LLM applications in a private corpus. Key decisions include chunking strategy, embedding model and refresh cadence, vector store choice, and retrieval quality evaluation. Typical pitfalls are stale indexes after source updates and poor retrieval quality masked by fluent generations.

name: LLM corpus preparation
summary: Cleaning, deduplication, and PII-scrubbing of text corpora for AI.

name: Embedding pipeline
summary: Batch and streaming embedding generation and refresh.

name: Recommender data infrastructure
summary: Interaction logs, candidate stores, and feedback loops.

name: Model & data drift monitoring
summary: Statistical monitoring of model inputs and outputs.

name: Experimentation / A-B platform
summary: Assignment, exposure logging, and a stats engine.

name: Tool evaluation / PoC
summary: Structured bake-off with criteria and a verdict.

name: Vendor selection
summary: RFP-style selection with scoring.

name: Data platform assessment / audit
summary: Health-check of an existing estate covering cost, risk, and debt.

name: Data strategy definition
summary: Target architecture plus capability roadmap.

name: Data mesh adoption
summary: Domain ownership, self-serve platform, and federated governance.

name: Data product definition
summary: Specifying a data product: contract, SLOs, and owners.

name: Data maturity assessment
summary: Scoring the organization against a maturity model.

name: Data team enablement / literacy
summary: Training and adoption programs.
